title: Tom Yum Goong
subtitle: Thai hot and sour prawn soup
excerpt: Thailand's signature soup: a fragrant, fiercely hot and sour broth of lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce, loaded with prawns and mushrooms. Extraordinarily quick to make once the aromatics are assembled.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tom yum goong (literally 'sour soup with prawns') is the national soup of Thailand and one of the most internationally recognised Thai dishes. Tom yum is classified as a hot and sour soup (distinct from tom kha, which uses coconut milk to temper the heat and acid), and is built on a base of fresh aromatics: lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fresh bird's eye chillies, simmered briefly in water or light stock, then seasoned with fish sauce and lime juice for the characteristic hot-sour-salty balance. The soup should be seasoned at the last moment; fish sauce and lime are volatile and the balance changes quickly with heat. Tom yum with coconut milk (tom yum nam khon) is a richer variation.

content.text: The aromatics are bruised and simmered to extract flavour but are not eaten; they are set aside before the prawns are added. The soup must be seasoned at the very last moment with fish sauce and lime: both flavours degrade with continued heat. Serve immediately. Bird's eye chillies give significant heat; reduce the quantity for a milder result.

items.preparation: bruised and cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Bring the stock to the boil. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chillies. Simmer for 5 minutes to infuse.
Add the mushrooms and cherry tomatoes. Simmer for 3 minutes. Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until they are pink and just cooked.

Remove from the heat. Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Taste and adjust; the soup should be sharply sour, saltily savory, and hot. Serve in deep bowls with spring onion and coriander. The lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves can be removed before serving or left for presentation.
